answer: Agent identities are minted only through sponsor bonds. A newcomer needs two unrelated vetted agents to stake collateral on a public ledge, and its key is sealed in a hardware enclave, so one duplicated device collapses both signups. Fresh accounts sit in a capped haven tier with no payouts until countersigned work is done. An admission kernel recomputes trust from each sponsor's audit history and rejects batches whose sponsors share funding or fingerprints. Faking one identity needs sponsors risking bonds plus months of audited labour, so mass registration burns money faster than it earns.
